paragraphs: He reported in the name of Rabbi Elazar (Bava Metzia 72b), and in the name of Rabbi Mani (Chullin 56b); the source also has א׳.

notes.text: The isolated א׳ after Rabbi Mani is preserved in the Hebrew and noted here; its function remains unclear. Chullin56b confirms that Rav Shmuel bar Chiyya reports Rabbi Mani.

The saved named Davidson Chullin 56b paragraph explicitly has Rav Shmuel bar Chiyya reporting Rabbi Mani, with the saying beginning אדומין. That incipit is a possible explanation for isolated א׳, but resemblance does not prove Hyman’s abbreviation practice or glyphs; the marker remains unresolved. No extra content is inserted and the Elazar attribution remains supplied.

Hyman’s printed entry (vol. III, p. 1136) has an א׳ after Rabbi Mani. In Chullin 56b the statement attributed to Mani begins אדומין (“red organs”), which may explain the letter. Bava Metzia 72b has Rabbi Shmuel bar Chiyya reporting Rabbi Elazar on borrowing produce; Chullin 56b calls the transmitter Rav Shmuel bar Chiyya and has him reporting Rabbi Mani.
